title: Rational and common-stage point evaluation normalization
statement:
Fix the point and coefficient data of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]: $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, and a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ inside a fixed $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$. Use the completed integral point category, its raw scalar localization at $\varpi_E$, and the common finite-stage category at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For $\Lambda=R,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $C_\Lambda\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], write $F_\Lambda=\operatorname{Fib}_s$, $c_\Lambda=F_\Lambda C_\Lambda$, $H_\Lambda=R\mathcal Hom_s(C_\Lambda,\Lambda_s)$, and $c_\Lambda^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(c_\Lambda,\Lambda)$. Define $\kappa_{\Lambda,C}:F_\Lambda H_\Lambda\to c_\Lambda^\vee$ as the transpose of $F_\Lambda(\operatorname{ev})$ through the tensor and unit comparisons [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Let $u_\Lambda:\omega_{s,\Lambda}\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$, $\rho_{\Lambda,C}=R\mathcal Hom_s(C_\Lambda,u_\Lambda)$ and $j_{\Lambda,C}:F_\Lambda R\mathcal Hom_s(C_\Lambda,\omega_{s,\Lambda})\to c_\Lambda^\vee$ be the specified point-dualizing comparisons [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex].
For an integral representative $C_R$ of $C_E$, put $c_R=F_RC_R$ and choose any bounded finite-projective complex $P$ representing $c_R$ [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Under the stipulated rationalization comparisons one has
$$\kappa_{E,C}=\delta_P\circ(\kappa_{R,C}\otimes_RE),\qquad F_E\rho_{E,C}=F_R\rho_{R,C}\otimes_RE,$$
where the perfect scalar-Hom isomorphism $\delta_P:P^\vee\otimes_RE\to(P\otimes_RE)^\vee$ [lem-pc-base-change-rhom-perfect] is the map $h\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto h(x)ab)$. The transpose uses the same signed evaluation $(-1)^{pj}$ for $x\in P^p$ and $h\in(P^\vee)^j$ on both sides. This is valid when the integral representative has torsion cohomology, and is natural for every localized morphism, including sums of $v\otimes a$.
For $E\subset L$ finite in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, these equations respect the specified sections scalar comparisons $\varphi$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and the internal-Hom comparison defined as transpose of scalar-extended evaluation. On perfect models its coefficient arrow is $P^\vee\otimes_R\mathcal O_L\to\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_L}^\bullet(P\otimes_R\mathcal O_L,\mathcal O_L)$, $h\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto h(x)ab)$, in the Hom convention [def-pur-hom-complex]. Compatibility includes identities and towers $E\subset L\subset M$ after rationalization. Consequently $\kappa_{\Lambda,C}$ is an isomorphism and $j_{\Lambda,C}=\kappa_{\Lambda,C}\circ F_\Lambda\rho_{\Lambda,C}$ for $\Lambda=E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, independent of the integral representative and the common finite field stage.

proof.text: First work with an arbitrary integral representative $C_R$. Apply [lem-pur-rational-lattice-adic-domain] with $T=s$, a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$: its integral category has exactly the objects of $D^b_c(s,\mathcal O_E)$, and every integral representative of a rational object, torsion ones included, lies in $D^b_{ctf}(s,R)$ with one Tor interval for all reductions. Apply [lem-pod-point-integral-evaluation-normalization]. It supplies the actual counit representative $L_RP\cong C_R$, with $P$ bounded finite projective, the evaluation-defined isomorphism $\kappa_{R,C}$, and $j_{R,C}=\kappa_{R,C}F_R\rho_{R,C}$. In its Hom-complex model the comparison is $h\mapsto(x\mapsto h(1\otimes x))$, and evaluation in the order $P\otimes P^\vee$ has sign $(-1)^{pj}$. These assertions concern the completed integral operations, and require no torsion-freeness of the cohomology of $P$.

source.place: Second sentence: coefficient Hom at the point; rationalization and common finite-stage normalization (agent expansion).

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-perfect-dual-scalar-calculus] to $R\to E$ and this $P$. Its isomorphism $\beta_{E/R,P}$ is $\delta_P$ of the statement: on homogeneous tensors it sends $h\otimes a$ to $(x\otimes b\mapsto h(x)ab)$. The rational operations extend the integral operations linearly by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom], and $F_E=F_R(-)\otimes_RE$ by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point]. The rational tensor and unit comparisons are the scalar extensions of the integral ones by [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]. Thus the uncurry of $\delta_P(\kappa_{R,C}\otimes_RE)$ is the scalar extension of integral evaluation: on $(x\otimes b)\otimes(h\otimes a)$ it is $(-1)^{pj}h(x)ab$. This is exactly the evaluation whose transpose defines $\kappa_{E,C}$. The two morphisms therefore agree by injectivity of the tensor–Hom adjunction bijection [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Both factors are isomorphisms, so $\kappa_{E,C}$ is an isomorphism in $D(E)$.

source.place: Second sentence: coefficient Hom at the point; rationalization and common finite-stage normalization (agent expansion).

proof.text:
For rationalization $Q_s$, [lem-pod-point-dual-coefficient-domains] gives the dualizing coefficient comparison normalized by $u_E$ to $Q_su_R$, with sections comparison equal to the identity under $F_E=F_R(-)\otimes_RE$. Applying the rational Hom formula of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] to this equality gives $F_E\rho_{E,C}=(F_R\rho_{R,C})\otimes_RE$. By the statement of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex], the comparison at $E$ is the rationalization of the integral one, with the point Hom computed over the coefficient ring. The rational coefficient arrow is fixed by [lem-pod-point-hom-rational-descent]: the composite of the rationalized integral Hom-complex comparison with the perfect-source base-change arrow, here $\delta_P$, is the isomorphism $F_E R\mathcal Hom_E(C_E,E_s)\to c_E^\vee$, independent of $P$. Its hypothesis that $H=R\mathcal Hom_B(C_R,B)$ is constructible with the finite-projective Hom model is [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation] for $P$. On the counit model of Step 1 that integral comparison is $\kappa_{R,C}$, so this arrow is $\delta_P(\kappa_{R,C}\otimes_RE)=\kappa_{E,C}$ by Step 2. Rationalizing the last equality in Step 1 therefore gives
$$j_{E,C}=\delta_P(j_{R,C}\otimes_RE)=\delta_P(\kappa_{R,C}\otimes_RE)(F_R\rho_{R,C}\otimes_RE)=\kappa_{E,C}F_E\rho_{E,C}.$$
Here the coefficient dual identification is the actual signed Hom-complex map of Step 2, rather than a chosen abstract isomorphism.

proof.text: Naturality holds for all localized morphisms, not only integral arrows. For an integral $v:C_R\to C'_R$, Step 1 is natural in $v$, and [lem-pod-perfect-dual-scalar-calculus] makes $\delta$ natural for the induced derived map on coefficient perfect complexes, independently of the models. For $v\otimes a$, the fibre map is $a(F_Rv\otimes1)$ by [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], and the internal-Hom map is precomposition by $v$ multiplied by $a$ by [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Precomposition with $a(F_Rv\otimes1)$ multiplies a functional by $a$, so the same scalar multiplies both sides of each naturality square. Addition gives the square for $\sum_i v_i\otimes a_i$. Balancing is the defining tensor-product relation in these localized Hom groups. In particular this covers localized isomorphisms between different integral representatives. Conjugating by such an isomorphism gives the same evaluation-defined comparison. No step replaced a torsion complex by its degreewise underived dual; all duals were computed on $P$.

source.place: Second sentence: coefficient Hom at the point; rationalization and common finite-stage normalization (agent expansion).

proof.text: Let $E\subset L$ be finite. In the counit model of Step 1 put $K=L_RP$ and $H=L_R(P^\vee)$. The isomorphism $H\cong R\mathcal Hom_B(K,B)$, constructibility of both models and of their evaluation tensor, and the completed evaluation normalization are exactly [lem-pod-point-completed-evaluation]. Hence [lem-pod-point-scalar-hom-evaluation] applies to these perfect models. Its commuting square uses exactly $\varphi$ of [lem-weil-point-sections-scalar-extension] and identifies the evaluation-transpose internal-Hom scalar arrow with $\beta_{\mathcal O_L/R,P}$. Its coefficient formula is $h\otimes a\mapsto(x\otimes b\mapsto h(x)ab)$ in the same signed Hom convention. Rationalizing that square and using Step 2 gives the asserted scalar compatibility of $\kappa_E$. For $\rho$, the dualizing normalization in [lem-pod-point-dual-coefficient-domains] identifies the extended $u_E$ with $u_L$; applying the internal-Hom functor gives the corresponding square for $\rho$. Substituting $j=\kappa F\rho$ gives its square as well. The scalar-Hom lemma includes identities, towers and localized naturality, while the sections lemma includes the precise associators for $\varphi$; thus these squares use the stipulated comparisons also for $E\subset L\subset M$.

source.place: Second sentence: coefficient Hom at the point; rationalization and common finite-stage normalization (agent expansion).

proof.text: Finally use the common-stage definition [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients] and the corresponding fibre and operations [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Represent an object by $(E,C_E)$ and its comparison by Step 2 at $E$. An input morphism is represented over one finite common extension $L$, where Step 4 proves naturality. Replacing it by a representative at $M\supset L$ preserves that square by Step 5. Two representatives which become equal at a further stage therefore give equal morphism classes. The identity and tower equations of Step 5 show that the resulting comparison is independent of the common field and respects composition. The stagewise inverses of $\kappa_E$ also respect transitions (invert the commuting squares), so define a two-sided inverse in the common-stage category. This class is the common-stage arrow of [lem-pod-point-hom-rational-descent], which equals $\kappa_E$ at the stage $E$ by Step 3 and which that statement makes independent of the stage and of the morphism representatives; this is the common-stage version of the comparison meant in [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. The equation $j=\kappa F\rho$ holds there because Step 3 proves it at each finite stage and Step 5 preserves it under extension. This proves all the asserted conclusions for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.
